title: Cabin Systems — Replacement of the Entertainment Head End Server by the Interim Standard
abstract: Replacement of the original entertainment head end server by the interim solid state unit, giving operators a supportable server while the storage technology of the original unit is out of repair.

sections.planning_reason: The rotating storage array in the original head end server reached the end of its supportable life with no repair source and no qualified drop-in drive. Server-attributed cabin defects had risen to 4.8 per thousand flight hours and the mean time between unscheduled removals had fallen to 2 100 hours. The interim unit is released to give operators a supportable server while the second generation architecture is still in development.
sections.description: The server is replaced by an interim unit built on solid state storage in the same chassis envelope. The rack partition D4420121334529 and the upper partition D4420125490996 are retained. The obsolete seat track cover D4420127529323 at the rack front is removed and the aperture is closed by the stowage bin item D4420129816843, secured with anchor nuts EN258434K3. Boot software LC5R2884353 and parameter set LC4RABC2783 are loaded to the new unit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on ground power and make the cabin systems safe. Get access to the equipment rack through the galley area. Remove the seat track cover D4420127529323 at the rack front and scrap it. Disconnect and remove the original server. Install the interim unit in the existing rack space using the retained partitions D4420121334529 and D4420125490996. Install the stowage bin item D4420129816843 to close the rack front aperture, using anchor nuts EN258434K3. Reconnect the interfaces and apply ground power to the cabin. Load boot software LC5R2884353 and parameter set LC4RABC2783 and confirm the reported part numbers. Do a full cabin entertainment functional check on at least ten seat groups per deck. Record the embodiment and return the removed server.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00122 at the original server standard. Aircraft above that serial were delivered with a later chassis and are outside the effectivity. The rack preparation is common, so an aircraft converted under this bulletin can be taken to any later server standard without further structural work.
sections.material_note: Kit K4420-1019-01 covers one aircraft and is available from June 2020. There is no long-lead item. Removed servers are returned to the supplier and are not available as spares.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled cabin systems access, or within 36 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

abstract: Replacement of the original entertainment head end server by the interim solid state unit. Cancelled in 2022 when the second generation architecture became available and made the interim step unnecessary for most operators.

sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00122 at the original server standard. This Service Bulletin is cancelled with effect from the release of the second generation architecture. Operators that have not accomplished it must not start it: the interim unit would be removed again at the next conversion, at the cost of a rack strip and a week of cabin downtime for nothing. The aircraft still open on this bulletin are notified directly by the field service organisation, because the revision service does not reach a planning department early enough to stop a slot that is already booked. Operators should go directly to the second generation architecture, which uses the same rack preparation and is covered by its own Service Bulletin.
sections.material_note: Kit K4420-1019-01 is withdrawn and is no longer supplied. Operators holding unused kits may return them for credit until the end of the warranty period. Removed servers were returned to the supplier and are not available as spares.

revision_history.reason: Service Bulletin cancelled; operators directed to the second generation architecture and notified directly
